newsitem.title: POLAND: NBP to collect deposits to offset govt loan.
newsitem.headline: NBP to collect deposits to offset govt loan.

text.p: Poland's central bank is ready to lend the government up to one billion zlotys for flood relief, but will collect deposits to offset the monetary effect of such a loan, the bank's deputy president said.

Witold Kozinski told a news conference the National Bank of Poland, which stopped commercial activities in 1993, would again offer individuals, firms or banks six- and nine-month deposits at competitive rates at its 49 outlets across the country.

"We are ready to offer the government a credit of up to one billion zlotys...this would be a credit solely for the removal of the flood damage and one should expect NBP efforts to neutralise its monetary impact," Kozinski said.
"Therefore, for a limited period when the credit is outstanding, the NBP would resume its deposit activity and accept deposits for six and nine months," he added.

On Monday Finance Minister Marek Belka said the government would seek to amend the 1997 budget to borrow one billion zlotys or more from the central bank to give it more flexibility in funding reconstruction efforts.

The government also wants to borrow $300 million from the World Bank and squeeze 500 to 700 million zlotys from the budget to deal with floods which inundated some 4,000 sq km in southern Poland, killing at least 36 people and causing huge damage to homes and infrastructure.

The method of raising the cash worried many economists who said a loan from the central bank and a foreign loan were pure creation of money which would have to be sterilised at a great cost. Instead they favoured a national loan or a flood tax.

"If the deposit collection succeeds the monetary effect (of the loan) will be neutral," Kozinski said, adding that interest on the deposits would be paid from interest on the government credit, which would also be "at market rates".
"As for the foreign loan, we will have to sterilise its monetary effect but we have large experience in that and it is not a cause for concern," he added.
Kozinski said that the deposit collection would allow Poland to keep its ambitious 13-percent year-on-year inflation target for this year and fast economic growth. @
"(Despite the flood situation) I think the 13 percent inflation target and fast economic growth this year are still possible," Kozinski said.
Kozinski said the NBP would use a special provision in its charter to take off the market the same amount of deposits that would be pumped into the system by its loan for the government.
He said the NBP would be able to offer competitive rates on its deposits, possibly above the 18-19 percent in annual terms now offered on deposits by commercial banks.
He said that full details of the government credit and NBP deposit arrangement would be announced when the bank reached a deal with the government.
